questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of these do you NOT need to adjust?

options.text: Tire pressure
Suspension
Headlight
Brake light

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You need to adjust tire pressure, suspension settings, and headlight position if needed. The brake light does not need adjustment.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because drivers will see you easily
No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you
Yes, because a passenger may tell the driver you are there
No, it is illegal and you must ride in the center of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining
Ride only on the oily strip because it gives better grip
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this strip usually still has enough grip for motorcycles. When wet, avoid it. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride beside it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed
Avoid making sudden moves
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are often more slippery.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what is the best lane position?

options.text: Always stay in one spot in the lane
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions
Only ride in the center so other drivers see you
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best or always bad. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is how many times more likely to survive a crash?

options.text: Two times
Three times
Six times
20 times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you turn?

options.text: Just your head
Your head and shoulders
Just your shoulders
Your entire body

questions.correctAnswerText: Just your head
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, keep your shoulders still, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it easily

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with the rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when either brake lever is used
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter
Connects the rear brake to a foot control
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when either brake lever is used
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either the front or rear brake, both brakes get pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group ride?

options.text: Just behind the leader
In front of the group
At the rear of the group
Beside the leader

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader, near the front of the group. This lets more experienced riders stay close and watch them.

questions.question: As an operator, what should you NOT tell a passenger to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Before starting, tell your passenger to get on only after the engine runs. They should sit close to you, not far away. Tell them to hold onto the handholds or your waist. Tell them to keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other hot or moving parts.

questions.question: What should you NOT do to avoid getting tired on a long ride?

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit how far you travel in one day.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: To stay safe and avoid fatigue, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than about six hours per day. Stop for a break at least once every two hours. Do not take artificial stimulants because you will feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When weight moves to the front of your bike during braking, what should you do?

options.text: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Do nothing. Weight transfer does not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: When you brake, slowly press harder on the front brake lever as the bike's weight moves forward to the front tire.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop completely.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.
questions.explanation: If your front tire locks while braking, release the brake lever so the tire can grip the road again. Then re-apply the brake.

questions.question: When it is raining, what is usually the best place to ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Pull off the road and wait for the rain to stop.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the road is very slippery. Oil from cars has not yet washed away. It is safest to ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often your best choice.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the leader.
Close to the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should be positioned just behind the leader. This way they will not have to rush to keep up. More experienced riders behind them can also watch them.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and your shoulders.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: To reduce your reaction time, cover the clutch and brakes. This is helpful when riding in areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.
